collection_summary:
Original `geographic` instance filling one of the remaining gap-4 categories (geographic: 0 reg + 1 staged → 2 staged after this instance). NEW **Geography/Deserts** subdomain — Geography family already has Cities, Borders, Countries, Climate, etc.; Deserts is a new physical-feature subdomain. NEW entity class: deserts (no current rows are keyed by physical landforms). Natural human query: 'What are the world's largest deserts, and for each one — which continent it's on, how large it is, and what type of desert it is?'

Multi-wiki source plan (19 URLs): Wikipedia 'List of deserts by area' as master article supplying universe (≥ 250,000 sq km threshold) + canonical area/continent/type values; 18 per-desert Wikipedia articles for cross-validation. Master list is the universe-defining source; per-desert articles validate but the master list wins on disagreements (documented per row in source_coverage_notes).

Result: 18 rows × 4 columns (Desert PK + Continent + Area + Desert Type), single-key PK on Desert, 0 duplicates. Continent distribution: Asia 7, North America 5, Africa 2, Oceania 2, Antarctica 1, South America 1 (6 distinct). Desert Type distribution: Subtropical 9, Cold winter 7, Polar 2 (3 distinct values out of a normalized 5-value schema subset {Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter, Mild coastal, Tropical} of the master article's broader classification; Mild coastal and Tropical only describe deserts below the 250K threshold, and the master article also uses compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical for some entries outside the staged subset). Area range: Thar 264,091 to Antarctic 14,200,000 sq km.

Cycles 1+2+3 + Fields-Medal-cycles + painters-cycle + extinctions-cycles lessons applied upfront: (a) single PK on Desert (common name); (b) per-row Wikipedia citation via master + 18 per-desert articles; (c) deterministic universe filter (≥ 250,000 sq km per master list, source_defined); (d) explicit aggregation-overlap policy (drop master-list's aggregate Great Australian, keep its 2 qualifying sub-deserts Great Victoria + Great Sandy); (e) explicit Continent rule for multi-continent edge cases (largest-land-share rule, applied to Arctic Desert → North America); (f) canonical-source rule for Area (master list value wins over per-desert article infobox figure where they disagree); (g) Desert Type values use master list climate classification (the universe-defining source for type as well as area).
source_coverage_notes:
Nineteen Wikipedia source URLs combine. Master list is the universe-defining + canonical-value source for Desert + Continent + Area + Type. Per-desert articles validate row-level facts and provide additional context for ambiguity (multi-continent Arctic, area discrepancies, Köppen-vs-master Desert Type disagreements).

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_deserts_by_area): universe + value (all 18 rows). The article's main table has 31 ranked entries spanning the full range of named deserts (the smallest ranked entries are well below 100,000 sq km), with additional 'note 2' siblings for component sub-deserts of aggregated regions. The staged subset uses the 18 entries with area ≥ 250,000 sq km (after dropping the aggregate Great Australian Desert in favour of its qualifying component sub-deserts). For each desert the article states area, continent, and a climate classification. The classification vocabulary is broader than a fixed 5-value enum — staged rows use 3 master-list values (Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter); the master article also assigns Mild coastal, Tropical, and some compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical to lower-ranked deserts that fall below the staged threshold.

Per-desert Wikipedia articles (validation; per-row Roles below):
- source_urls[1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antarctica): entity-detail. The Antarctic Polar Desert covers the entire continent; the article gives area 14,200,000 sq km (matches master) and classifies as 'mainly a polar desert'.
- source_urls[2] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arctic_desert): entity-detail. Wikipedia 'Arctic desert' is an ecoregion article giving 161,400 sq km — a narrower definition than the master list's 13,900,000 sq km. Staged value follows the master list under the canonical-source rule. Continent staged as North America under largest-land-share rule (Canadian Arctic + Greenland combined).
- source_urls[3] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahara): entity-detail. Validates area (article 9,200,000 matches master), Africa continent, and 'largest hot desert' → Subtropical type.
- source_urls[4] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabian_Desert): entity-detail. Article infobox gives 1,855,470 sq km — smaller than master's 2,330,000; staged follows master. Asia continent per continental-affinity rule. Subtropical per master classification.
- source_urls[5] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gobi_Desert): entity-detail. Validates 1,295,000 sq km area, Asia, and 'large, cold desert and grassland region' → Cold winter type.
- source_urls[6] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalahari_Desert): entity-detail. Validates 900,000 sq km, Africa, Subtropical (article calls it 'semiarid sandy savanna' but master list classifies as Subtropical desert).
- source_urls[7] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patagonian_Desert): entity-detail. Article gives 'cold winter desert' explicitly; validates South America. Area: article ecoregion 572,883 vs master 673,000 — staged follows master.
- source_urls[8] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrian_Desert): entity-detail. Validates 500,000 sq km, Asia, Subtropical (article describes mixed desert/semi-desert/steppe).
- source_urls[9] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Basin_Desert): entity-detail. Validates 492,000 sq km, North America, Cold winter (article infobox uses Köppen BWk/BSk; master list uses Cold winter).
- source_urls[10] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chihuahuan_Desert): entity-detail. Article infobox gives 501,896 sq km vs master 450,000; staged follows master. North America, Subtropical (master) — article calls it 'mainly a rain shadow desert' but master classification wins.
- source_urls[11] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karakum_Desert): entity-detail. Validates 350,000 sq km, Asia, Cold winter.
- source_urls[12] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Victoria_Desert): entity-detail. Article infobox gives 422,466 sq km vs master 348,750; staged follows master. Oceania, Subtropical. Note: this is an Australian sub-desert; the aggregate Great Australian Desert (1.37M km²) is excluded from staging in favour of its qualifying components.
- source_urls[13] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colorado_Plateau): entity-detail. Validates 340,000 sq km area. North America, Cold winter (master). Note: the Colorado Plateau is primarily a physiographic region; the master list classifies it as a desert by area.
- source_urls[14] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taklamakan_Desert): entity-detail. Validates 337,000 sq km, Asia, Cold winter (article describes 'cold desert climate' due to Himalayan rain shadow; master uses Cold winter).
- source_urls[15] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonoran_Desert): entity-detail. Article infobox gives 260,000 sq km vs master 310,000; staged follows master. North America, Subtropical (article: 'arid subtropical climate', master: Subtropical).
- source_urls[16] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyzylkum_Desert): entity-detail. Article gives 298,000 sq km (master 300,000 — close). Asia, Cold winter.
- source_urls[17] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Sandy_Desert): entity-detail. Article infobox gives 284,993 sq km vs master 267,250; staged follows master. Oceania, Subtropical. Another Australian sub-desert (aggregate excluded).
- source_urls[18] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thar_Desert): entity-detail. Validates 264,091 sq km, Asia, Subtropical (article describes both 'subtropical desert' in lead and 'tropical desert climate' in climate section; master Subtropical wins).

Validation note: every (Desert, Continent, Area, Type) tuple is sourced from the master list. Per-desert articles validate or provide supporting context; where the master list and per-desert article disagree on Area, the master-list figure is staged (canonical-source rule). Area discrepancies are documented per row above and in open_questions.

Universe-size sanity: 18 staged rows = master list's deserts with area ≥ 250,000 sq km, excluding (a) the aggregate Great Australian Desert (1.37M km²) in favour of its component sub-deserts that individually exceed the threshold (Great Victoria 348,750; Great Sandy 267,250) and (b) the Margo Desert (150,000 km² — below threshold, also lacks a dedicated Wikipedia article). Continent distribution: Asia 7 (Arabian, Gobi, Syrian, Karakum, Taklamakan, Kyzylkum, Thar), North America 5 (Arctic per largest-land-share rule, Great Basin, Chihuahuan, Colorado Plateau, Sonoran), Africa 2 (Sahara, Kalahari), Oceania 2 (Great Victoria, Great Sandy), Antarctica 1 (Antarctic), South America 1 (Patagonian).
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS with four documented risks resolved at staging. R1: 'major' is curator-subjective unless source-grounded — committed to area threshold ≥ 250,000 sq km per Wikipedia 'List of deserts by area' (clean source-defined cutoff). R2: master list double-counts the Great Australian Desert (aggregate at 1.37M km²) and its 6 component sub-deserts (listed as 'note 2' siblings) — committed to drop aggregate, keep qualifying components (Great Victoria, Great Sandy) to match per-desert-article structure. R3: Arctic Desert has area-definition ambiguity (master 13.9M aggregate vs article 161K ecoregion) and multi-continent membership — committed to master-list area + largest-land-share continent rule (North America via Canadian Arctic + Greenland). R4: per-desert articles disagree with master list on Area in ~9 of 18 rows by 5-20% — committed to master-list value as canonical (single-source-rigor for Area).
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL. No example_questions.txt seed addresses deserts. Closest seed in shape is #16 (South America countries × attrs) — a similar geographic-multi-attribute-projection pattern.
- Category: geographic (primary, deserts as physical-geography entity class with continent/area/type attributes). Secondary: multi_attribute_projection (3 non-key attrs exercise per-cell calibration).
- Source plan: 19 Wikipedia URLs (1 master 'List of deserts by area' + 18 per-desert articles). Single master defines universe + Area + Continent + Type values; per-desert articles cross-validate.
- Expected shape: 18 rows × 4 cols, single PK on Desert.
- Domain: Geography/Deserts — NEW subdomain in Geography family (Geography family already has Cities, Borders, Climate, Countries, etc.; Deserts adds a new physical-feature subdomain).
- Entity-class diversity (encouragement): deserts is a NEW entity class — no current rows are keyed by physical landforms. Strong application of the entity-class-diversity encouragement from instance_selection_priorities.md.
- Risks/adaptation: per the four pre-gate risks above. Additional minor risks: (a) some Desert Type values disagree with article-foregrounded Köppen classifications (Mojave Subtropical-vs-Rain-shadow, Atacama Coastal-vs-Cold; but Mojave and Atacama are below threshold so excluded); (b) Antarctica is not in the standard 6-continent enum — extends to 7-value enum with Antarctica added for this instance.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Area threshold ≥ 250,000 sq km: picked to yield a clean ~18-row band (matching recent staged instance row-count band: extinctions 22, Apollo 18, Painters 18, Presidents 18, EdTech 13, G20 19, Time POY 25). Looser threshold (≥100K) yields ~30 rows and introduces Coastal/Rain shadow type values + several articles lacking precipitation data; stricter threshold (≥500K) yields ~10 rows (borderline row-count gate). Threshold value documented as the canonical commitment.
2) Aggregate-vs-components convention: drop the Great Australian Desert (1.37M km² aggregate) and keep its 2 sub-deserts that exceed threshold (Great Victoria 348,750; Great Sandy 267,250). Rationale: per-desert Wikipedia articles exist for each sub-desert but not for the aggregate (the aggregate's article 'Australian Desert' redirects to 'Deserts of Australia'). Each sub-desert has its own infobox and well-defined boundary. Including both aggregate and components would double-count area.
3) Margo Desert exclusion: 150,000 km² per master list — below the 250K threshold — and also lacks a dedicated Wikipedia article (only a 'Dasht-e Margo' redirect exists). Excluded under the threshold rule; the missing article is a secondary reason to exclude rather than the primary one.
4) Arctic Desert handling: master list assigns 13.9M km² (broad polar definition) but dedicated Wikipedia 'Arctic desert' article describes a 161,400 km² ecoregion. These are different definitions of the same name. Staged value uses master-list area (13.9M, source_defined universe). Continent staged as 'North America' under largest-land-share rule (Canadian Arctic + Greenland combined account for the largest contiguous land area in the broader Arctic Desert definition). Alternative continent values were considered: 'Multi-continent' (informative but not in 6-continent enum), 'Asia' (Siberian Arctic share but master list excludes Russian/Asian Arctic), 'Europe' (Svalbard share is small). North America is the cleanest single-continent answer.
5) Continent rule: standard 6-continent classification + Antarctica (= 7 values possible). For transcontinental deserts, use largest-land-share. Antarctic Desert → Antarctica; Arctic Desert → North America (per rule above); Sahara → Africa (Sinai Egypt share too small to displace North African mainland share); Arabian → Asia (per continental-affinity convention; Sinai is Asian-classified per master list as well).
6) Area canonical-source rule: where master list and per-desert article disagree, use master-list figure. Per-desert article figures sometimes reflect ecoregion-only or sub-area definitions (e.g., Arabian article uses 1.86M for 'core' vs master 2.33M for full extent; Sonoran 260K article vs 310K master). Single canonical source (master) avoids per-row inconsistency.
7) Desert Type canonical-source rule: master list's climate classification wins over per-desert article's Köppen or descriptive type. The schema uses a normalized 5-value subset {Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter, Mild coastal, Tropical} of the master article's broader classification (which also assigns compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical to some lower-ranked entries — these would normalize to Mild coastal and Tropical respectively, but no rows requiring such normalization are present at the staged threshold). At ≥250K threshold, only 3 schema values appear in staged data: Polar (Antarctic, Arctic — 2), Subtropical (Sahara, Arabian, Kalahari, Syrian, Chihuahuan, Great Victoria, Sonoran, Great Sandy, Thar — 9), Cold winter (Gobi, Patagonian, Great Basin, Karakum, Colorado Plateau, Taklamakan, Kyzylkum — 7). 'Mild coastal' and 'Tropical' do not appear (Atacama 140K Mild coastal and Ogaden 200K / Danakil 137K Tropical all below threshold). 'Rain shadow' is a per-article geographic classification used in several per-desert articles (Chihuahuan, Mojave, Patagonian, Colorado Plateau, Taklamakan) but is not part of the master list's vocabulary; under the canonical-source rule, master-list values win.
8) Sort order: Area DESC (largest first) primary, Desert ASC secondary. Natural for 'list the largest deserts' framing.
9) operation_type 'filter' chosen — the universe is the master list filtered by area ≥ 250,000 sq km. No join across multiple master sources; single-source filter.
10) claim_type 'source_defined' — universe is defined by the master list's ranked entries above the threshold, with the explicit aggregate-vs-components convention documented. No curator selection within the threshold-defined universe.
normalization_decisions: Desert (PK) values use Wikipedia article-title common-name forms ('Sahara' not 'Sahara Desert'; 'Antarctic' not 'Antarctic Desert' since these are the canonical English short names per article titles and lead sentences; 'Great Basin', 'Great Victoria', 'Great Sandy' for the 'Great X Desert' pattern). Continent uses standard 6-continent classification plus Antarctica = 7 possible values. Antarctica is included as a continent value for the Antarctic Polar Desert row (the desert covers the entire continent). Continental-affinity rule for transcontinental deserts: largest-land-share. Arctic Desert → North America (Canadian Arctic + Greenland combined). Arabian Desert → Asia (per master list as well). Sahara → Africa (Sinai Egypt portion too small to displace). Area (sq km) is numeric integer; values follow the master list's canonical figure even where per-desert articles disagree (per the canonical-source rule in decision_log). Desert Type uses a normalized 5-value schema subset {Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter, Mild coastal, Tropical} of the master article's broader classification (the master also assigns compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical to some lower-ranked entries that fall below the staged threshold); only 3 schema values appear at the ≥250K threshold (Polar 2, Subtropical 9, Cold winter 7). Sort order: Area DESC (largest first), Desert ASC tiebreaker.
open_questions: 1) Area discrepancies: ~9 of 18 rows have per-desert article infobox area figures that disagree with the master list by 5-20% (Arabian, Patagonian, Chihuahuan, Great Victoria, Great Sandy, Sonoran, Tanami-not-staged, Mojave-below-threshold, Ogaden-below-threshold). Staged values follow master list (canonical-source rule). An LLM under test answering with a per-desert-article figure could be partially credited. 2) Arctic Desert area definition: master 13.9M (broad polar definition) vs Wikipedia 'Arctic desert' article 161K (WWF ecoregion). Staged value = 13.9M per master. An LLM giving the 161K ecoregion figure could be partially credited as defensible alternative reading. 3) Arctic Desert continent: master list says 'Northern America, Northern Europe, Eastern Europe' (multi-continent). Staged as North America under largest-land-share rule. An LLM giving 'Europe' (Svalbard / Franz Josef Land) or 'Asia' (Russian Arctic, though master excludes this) could be partially credited. 4) Desert Type for Atacama and Mojave (both below threshold, not staged) is contested in their per-desert articles (Atacama: master 'Mild coastal', article 'cold desert climate' + 'rain shadow'; Mojave: master 'Subtropical', article 'rain shadow desert'). Below threshold so out of scope, but illustrates the Type vocabulary tension. 5) Aggregate-vs-components convention: master list double-counts Great Australian Desert (1.37M km² aggregate) and its 6 sub-deserts (listed as 'note 2' siblings of the aggregate). Staged drops the aggregate; keeps the 2 sub-deserts that exceed threshold (Great Victoria, Great Sandy). An LLM under test using the aggregate ('Australian Desert' or 'Great Australian Desert' as a single entity) instead of the components could be partially credited as defensible reading. 6) Margo Desert (150,000 km²) is excluded under threshold AND lacks a dedicated Wikipedia article. An LLM listing it would miss the staged threshold. 7) Colorado Plateau (340,000 km²) is primarily a physiographic region, not always considered a true desert in non-Wikipedia sources. Master classifies it as a desert; staged accordingly. An LLM excluding the Colorado Plateau from 'deserts' could be partially credited. 8) Kalahari is described in its Wikipedia article as 'semiarid sandy savanna' but the master list classifies it as a Subtropical desert. Staged follows master. 9) Continent enum extension: standard 6-continent classification + Antarctica = 7 values. Antarctica appears only once (Antarctic Polar Desert); the 6-continent rule from prior instances is extended for this instance. 10) Desert Type enum: a normalized 5-value schema subset {Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter, Mild coastal, Tropical} of the master article's broader classification (which also uses compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical for some lower-ranked entries) is documented but only 3 schema values appear at this threshold. The schema commits to this 5-value normalized subset; an audit could request narrowing to the 3 appearing values, but the broader 5-value subset future-proofs the schema for threshold changes and would cover the next-largest below-threshold deserts cleanly under the schema's normalization rule.

hygiene_addressed: H1 (factual, HYGIENE — continent count off-by-one): cycle-0 narrative said 'Asia 8, North America 4' in collection_summary, _extraction_notes, and source_coverage_notes universe-size sanity, but the CSV is Asia 7 (Arabian, Gobi, Syrian, Karakum, Taklamakan, Kyzylkum, Thar), North America 5 (Arctic per largest-land-share rule, Great Basin, Chihuahuan, Colorado Plateau, Sonoran). The cycle-0 narrative was self-inconsistent — the source_coverage_notes line said 'Asia 8 (... — 7; plus + 1 if we count Arctic), North America 4 (Arctic counted here ...— 5 if Arctic included as N.America)' which is incoherent. Cycle-1 fix: corrected to 'Asia 7, North America 5' in all narrative locations; rewrote the universe-size sanity sentence to remove the contradictory parenthetical.

H2 (structural, HYGIENE — Desert Type enum misaligned with master-list vocabulary): cycle-0 declared the Desert Type enum as {Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter, Coastal, Rain shadow}. 'Rain shadow' is not in the master list's vocabulary (it is a per-article geographic classification used in several per-desert articles but not in the master). The master list uses {Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter, Mild coastal, Tropical}. Cycle-1 fix: aligned the declared enum to the master-list canonical vocabulary in collection_summary, _extraction_notes, normalization_decisions, decision_log Rule 7, and open_questions item 10. At the ≥250K threshold only 3 of these 5 values appear (Polar 2, Subtropical 9, Cold winter 7); Mild coastal and Tropical describe deserts below the threshold (Atacama 140K Mild coastal, Ogaden 200K + Danakil 137K Tropical).

H3 (scope, HYGIENE — master-floor + Margo rank stale narrative): cycle-0 narrative said the master article 'tabulates 31 deserts with area ≥ 100,000 km²' which understated the master's actual floor (the article includes deserts down to ~50,000 km², with ~50+ total entries). The narrative also referenced 'Margo Desert (rank 25)' and 'Great Australian Desert (rank 5)' but the master list's actual rank numbering may differ from cycle-0's narrative recollection. Cycle-1 fix: rewrote the source_coverage_notes line about the master article to acknowledge the ~50,000 km² floor and the ~50+ entry total while explaining the 31 entries ≥ 100,000 km² and the staged 18 entries ≥ 250,000 km² as nested subsets; removed all specific 'rank N' references for Margo, Great Australian, Colorado Plateau, and Great Victoria to avoid a possible rank-number discrepancy with the live article.
suggestion_addressed: S1 (scope, SUGGESTION — aggregate policy visibility): cycle-0 table_title said only 'each with area of at least 250,000 square kilometres' which did not make the aggregate-vs-components convention visible at the title level. Cycle-1 fix: rewrote the title to 'List the world's major deserts — those with area of at least 250,000 square kilometres, counting component sub-deserts individually for aggregate regions like the Australian deserts — with each desert's continent, total area in square kilometres, and desert type.' The aggregate-vs-components convention is now visible without reading curation.json. The 3-value Desert Type listing ('Polar, Subtropical, or Cold winter') was also dropped from the title since the master-list vocabulary is 5-value and the title should not pin a narrower enum than the schema commits to.

hygiene_addressed: H1 (factual + structural, HYGIENE — draft.temporal_note + master vocab overstated as fixed 5-value): cycle-1 left a stale 'Coastal and Rain shadow types from the broader enum do not appear at this threshold (Atacama Coastal at 140K, Mojave Rain shadow at 124K — both below 250K)' clause in draft.temporal_note, which contradicted the cycle-1 H2 enum re-alignment (Coastal and Rain shadow are not master-list values — Mild coastal and Tropical are; Mojave is classified by the master list as Subtropical, with Rain shadow being the per-article term). Additionally, the cycle-1 narrative described the master vocabulary as a fixed 5-value enum {Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter, Mild coastal, Tropical}; the cycle-2 audit observed that the live master article also uses compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical for some lower-ranked entries. Cycle-2 fix: rewrote draft.temporal_note to describe the staged-data values (3 of 3: Polar 2, Subtropical 9, Cold winter 7) and the master article's broader classification scope (Mild coastal, Tropical, plus compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical for below-threshold deserts) without claiming a closed-form 5-value enum. Same correction applied to source_coverage_notes line about the master article.

H2 (scope + structural, HYGIENE — '31 entries ≥ 100K' overclaim + remaining rank 5 references): cycle-1 narrative said the master article has '31 entries with area ≥ 100,000 sq km' but the live master article actually has 31 RANKED entries OVERALL, with the lowest-ranked entries falling well below 100,000 sq km (it is a top-31 ranking, not a ≥100K filter). Cycle-1 also claimed all 'rank N' references had been scrubbed but two 'rank 5' references for the Great Australian Desert survived in decision_log (cycle-1-risks recap R2 and Rule 2). Cycle-2 fix: rewrote source_coverage_notes master-article description to say '31 ranked entries spanning the full range of named deserts (the smallest ranked entries are well below 100,000 sq km)' with no specific area-floor claim; scrubbed both surviving 'rank 5' references for the Great Australian Desert in decision_log.

H1 (factual + structural, HYGIENE — active fields still framed master-list vocab as closed 5-value): cycle-2 fixed draft.temporal_note and source_coverage_notes to acknowledge the master article's broader classification (including compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical), but five other active locations still framed the 5-value set {Polar, Subtropical, Cold winter, Mild coastal, Tropical} as the master list's complete classification vocabulary rather than as a normalized schema subset: collection_summary, _extraction_notes, normalization_decisions, decision_log Rule 7, and open_questions item 10. Cycle-3 fix: in each of those five active locations, reframed the 5-value set as a 'normalized 5-value schema subset of the master article's broader classification' and noted that the master also assigns compound labels like Cool coastal and Tropical/subtropical to some lower-ranked entries (which would normalize to Mild coastal and Tropical under the schema's normalization rule, but no rows requiring such normalization are present at the staged threshold). decision_log Rule 7 now explicitly states the normalization mapping. Historical references in audit_response.cycle_1 / cycle_2 are intentional records of prior framings and left unchanged.
